docs.title: templatevue
docs.text: Copier template for Vue 3 + TypeScript apps deployed with Docker.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text: Tool Role pnpm Fast, disk-efficient package manager vite Build tool and dev server vue-tsc Type checking for Vue SFCs (.vue files) ESLint flat config Linting (@eslint/js, typescript-eslint, eslint-plugin-vue) Prettier Formatting (TS, Vue, JSON, Markdown, YAML) vitest Unit testing husky + lint-staged Git hooks: auto-fix staged files, validate commit message commitlint Enforces Conventional Commits message format release-it Conventional-commit version bump + tag (run in CI by versioning.yml) nginx Static file serving in production Docker + Compose Containerised deployment VitePress Project documentation

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Node.js — generated projects default to 24 (node_requires: choices 20 / 22 / 24)
  • pnpm ≥ 9 (npm install -g pnpm)
  • copier ≥ 9.0 (uv tool install copier)
  • Docker (for container builds)

docs.title: Create a new project
docs.text:
copier copy gh:larsrollik/templatevue my-new-project
cd my-new-project
git init && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: initial commit from templatevue"
pnpm install    # installs deps and sets up husky hooks via prepare script
cp .env.example .env
pnpm dev        # http://localhost:5173

docs.title: Template questions
docs.text: Question Choices / default Notes project_name free text Display name project_slug free text Package/directory name (kebab-case) project_pascal free text PascalCase name project_description free text One line author_name free text author_email free text github_username free text GitHub org or account github_repo free text Repository name node_requires 20 / 22 / 24, default 24 Node.js version the generated project targets traefik_host free text Traefik router host for deployment secret_config_path path Runtime config.json secret mount path year free text Copyright year license_type noncommercial (default) / bsd3 Licence for the generated project

docs.title: Apply template updates to an existing project
docs.text:
cd my-existing-project
copier update

docs.title: Day-to-day commands
docs.text:
pnpm dev            # vite dev server (serves public/config.json at /config.json)
pnpm build          # typecheck + vite build → dist/
pnpm test           # vitest in watch mode
pnpm test:run       # single run with coverage
pnpm lint           # eslint --fix
pnpm format         # prettier --write .
pnpm typecheck      # vue-tsc --build --force
pnpm docs:dev       # vitepress dev server
pnpm release --ci   # manual release override (bump + tag + push).
                    # Releases run automatically in CI on merge to main —
                    # this is only for a manual/off-cycle cut.

docs.text:
my-project/
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts          # createApp + loadConfig before mount
│   ├── App.vue          # root component
│   └── config.ts        # runtime config loader (fetches /config.json)

│   └── App.test.ts

├── docker/

├── docs/

docs.title: Branch protection
docs.text: Configure branch protection rules on GitHub to enforce the gitflow.

docs.title: Recommended rules for main
docs.text:
Repository → Settings → Branches → Add rule, branch name pattern: main

Setting Value Reason Require a pull request before merging ✓ No direct pushes to main Required approvals 1+ At least one review Dismiss stale reviews on new commits ✓ Re-review after force-push Require status checks to pass ✓ Blocks merge on CI failure Required status checks CI The aggregate job in ci.yml Require branches to be up to date ✓ No stale merges Restrict who can push maintainers only Prevents accidental direct pushes

docs.title: Allow versioning.yml to push back to main
docs.text:
There is no prod branch. On merge, versioning.yml commits the version bump and pushes the tag back to main. GitHub's default branch protection blocks this.

Note

If you require pull requests on main, add a bypass rule for the github-actions[bot] actor (GitHub's branch protection UI supports this), or the bump push will fail with a 403.

docs.title: Required status check name
docs.text: The aggregate job in ci.yml is named CI. This is what to enter in the required status checks field. It only passes when both lint and test succeed, and only runs when both have completed.

docs.title: Rulesets (modern alternative)
docs.text: GitHub now offers Rulesets (Repository → Settings → Rules → Rulesets) as a more flexible replacement for classic branch protection. Rulesets support bypass lists, actor-based rules, and can be applied to tag patterns too (useful for protecting v* tags from deletion).

docs.title: Docker deployment
docs.text: The app is served as a static SPA behind nginx in a multi-stage Docker image. Traefik handles TLS termination and routing in front.

docs.title: Image build
docs.text:
docker build -t myapp .

The Dockerfile has two stages:

Stage Base What it does build node:[[ node_requires ]]-alpine Installs deps, runs pnpm build, produces dist/ serve nginx:alpine Copies dist/ and nginx config; runs the runtime config hook

docs.title: Runtime config injection
docs.text:
At container startup, /docker-entrypoint.d/40-runtime-config.sh runs before nginx. If a secrets file is present at SECRET_CONFIG_PATH, it is copied to /usr/share/nginx/html/config.json, replacing the baked-in default.

The SECRET_CONFIG_PATH environment variable defaults to the value set during template generation. Override it in docker-compose.yml or pass it at docker run time.

# Mount a secrets file and start
docker run \
  -e SECRET_CONFIG_PATH=/run/secrets/myapp-config.json \
  -v /path/to/myapp-config.json:/run/secrets/myapp-config.json:ro \
  -p 80:80 \
  myapp

docs.title: Changing the injection logic
docs.text:
To replace the injection script without rebuilding the image, override it in docker-compose.yml:

volumes:
  - ./my-inject.sh:/docker-entrypoint.d/40-runtime-config.sh:ro

Your script runs in place of the default one; call /docker-entrypoint.sh at the end if you want to chain into nginx's own init sequence.

docs.title: Config tiers
Traefik
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml attaches the container to an external traefik network and sets the routing labels. Assumes Traefik is already running in a separate stack with a websecure entrypoint and a configured cert resolver.

Required labels (pre-filled from copier answers):

traefik.enable: "true"
traefik.http.routers.<slug>.rule: "Host(`<traefik_host>`)"
traefik.http.routers.<slug>.entrypoints: websecure
traefik.http.routers.<slug>.tls: "true"
traefik.http.services.<slug>.loadbalancer.server.port: "80"

docs.title: Local dev without Docker
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env      # edit VITE_* values as needed
pnpm dev                  # serves at http://localhost:5173
                          # public/config.json is served at /config.json

docs.title: GPG signing
docs.text: Signing commits and tags is optional but recommended for open-source projects. GitHub shows a "Verified" badge on signed commits.

docs.title: Generate a key
docs.text:
gpg --full-generate-key

Recommended options:

  • Key type: (9) ECC (sign and encrypt) → Curve 25519
  • Expiry: 2y (rotate every two years)
  • Name and email matching your GitHub account

docs.title: Find your key ID
docs.text:
gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format LONG

Output:

sec   ed25519/<KEY_ID> 2024-01-01 [SC] [expires: 2026-01-01]
      ABCDEF1234567890ABCDEF1234567890ABCDEF12
uid   [ultimate] Your Name <you@example.com>
ssb   cv25519/<SUBKEY_ID> 2024-01-01 [E]

The <KEY_ID> is the 16-character hex string after ed25519/.

docs.title: Configure git to use the key
docs.text:
git config --global user.signingkey <KEY_ID>
git config --global commit.gpgsign true
git config --global tag.gpgSign true

docs.title: Add the public key to GitHub
docs.text:
gpg --armor --export <KEY_ID>

Copy the output (including -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----).

Go to GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New GPG key and paste it.

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text:
GPG hangs and never asks for passphrase

export GPG_TTY=$(tty)

Add this to your shell profile (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc) to make it permanent.

error: gpg failed to sign the data

gpgconf --kill gpg-agent
gpg-agent --daemon

Wrong key used / multiple keys

Check which key git is using:

git config --global user.signingkey

List all available secret keys:

gpg --list-secret-keys

Key expired

Extend expiry without creating a new key:

gpg --edit-key <KEY_ID>
# at the gpg> prompt:
expire
# follow prompts, then:
save
# re-export and update the key on GitHub
gpg --armor --export <KEY_ID>

docs.title: Disabling signing temporarily
docs.text:
git commit --no-gpg-sign -m "message"
git tag --no-sign v1.0.0

Or disable globally:

git config --global commit.gpgsign false
git config --global tag.gpgSign false

docs.title: Local CI with act
docs.text: act runs GitHub Actions workflows locally using Docker. Useful for debugging CI without pushing.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# macOS
brew install act

# Linux
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nektos/act/master/install.sh | sudo bash

# Windows (winget)
winget install nektos.act

Requires Docker Desktop to be running.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Run all workflows triggered by push
act push

# Run a specific workflow
act push -W .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Run with verbose output
act push --verbose

# List available workflows and jobs
act -l

# Run a specific job
act push -j lint

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
On first run, act asks which Docker image size to use:

  • Micro — minimal, fast to download, may lack some tools
  • Medium — recommended for most workflows
  • Large — full GitHub Actions environment, ~20 GB

For this template's workflows, Medium is sufficient.

docs.title: Passing secrets locally
docs.text:
Most workflows need no secrets locally — the release image push uses GITHUB_TOKEN (provided automatically in CI). To test a job that needs a token:

act push --secret GITHUB_TOKEN=<token>
# or using a secrets file:
act push --secret-file .env.act

.env.act format (add to .gitignore):

GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_...
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• act doesn't support all GitHub Actions features (e.g. workflow_run, some contexts)
  • Some actions that call back to GitHub APIs may behave differently
  • Docker build/push jobs may need extra buildx/registry setup under act

docs.title: Release workflow
docs.text: Releases are automated in CI on merge to main — there is no prod branch and no manual release step. versioning.yml bumps + tags; release.yml builds the image and cuts the GitHub release.

docs.title: Branch topology
docs.text:
main  ←── PR merges from feature/bug/hotfix branches
feature/*, bug/*, hotfix/*  ←── created from main

docs.title: Step-by-step
docs.text:
# 1. Create a branch
git checkout main && git pull
git checkout -b feature/my-feature

# 2. Commit — message format enforced by the commitlint hook
git commit -m "feat: add dashboard view"

# 3. Push + open PR to main
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create --base main --title "feat: add dashboard view"

# 4. CI runs lint + typecheck on push; tests on PR — merge is blocked until green
# 5. Merge PR
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch

# 6. versioning.yml fires on push to main:
#    - release-it reads commits since the last tag, determines the increment,
#      commits "chore: release vX.Y.Z", tags it, and pushes
#    - dispatches release.yml

# 7. release.yml (on the tag / dispatch):
#    - builds the Docker image
#    - pushes to GHCR (ghcr.io/<org>/<repo>:<version>, :<major.minor>, :latest)
#    - creates a GitHub release with auto-generated notes

docs.title: How the version increment is determined
docs.text:
release-it with @release-it/conventional-changelog reads commits since the last tag:

Commits contain Bump only fix:, docs:, chore:, refactor:, test: patch 0.0.x at least one feat: minor 0.x.0 BREAKING CHANGE: footer or feat!:/fix!: major x.0.0

If there are no bumpable commits since the last tag, versioning.yml makes no change and nothing is released. To cut a release manually (or override the increment), run locally and push the tag — a hand-pushed tag triggers release.yml directly:

pnpm release --ci                     # bump from commits, tag, push
pnpm release --ci --increment minor   # force a specific increment

docs.title: Image tags produced
docs.text:
Each release pushes three tags to GHCR:

Tag Example Use Full semver v1.2.3 Pin to exact release Major.minor 1.2 Rolling minor updates latest latest Always current

docs.title: Conventional Commits format
docs.text:
commitlint (via the commit-msg husky hook) rejects non-conforming messages:

<type>[optional scope]: <short description>

[optional body]

[optional footer: BREAKING CHANGE: ...]

Common types: feat, fix, docs, chore, refactor, test, ci, build, style.

docs.title: Pre-commit auto-fix
docs.text:
The pre-commit hook runs lint-staged:

  1. eslint --fix on staged .ts and .vue files
  2. prettier --write on all staged files
  3. Re-stages auto-fixed files

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text:
versioning.yml didn't release after a merge

  • No bumpable commits since the last tag → nothing to release (expected).
  • Actions can't push to main → allow github-actions[bot] to bypass branch protection (see Branch protection).

commitlint rejects a message

Common mistakes: missing space after the colon (feat:message), uppercase type (Feat:), trailing period on the subject.
